name: stos-studio
description: Write STOS BASIC (Atari ST) in VS Code: command help, labels and includes, build to a numbered .asc and run it in the Hatari emulator.
author: Dimitris Filios

action.description: build: .stos -> .asc; run: build, then start Hatari

stosStudio.sourceFile.description: Main .stos file of the project, relative to the project folder.

stosStudio.outputFile.description: The numbered .asc file that is created, relative to the project folder. Must be inside the project folder.

stosStudio.hatariPath.markdownDescription:
Hatari program. Empty = default for your system (macOS: `/Applications/Hatari.app/Contents/MacOS/Hatari`).

[Select Hatari...](command:stosStudio.selectHatari) (on macOS you can pick `Hatari.app`).

stosStudio.tosImage.markdownDescription:
TOS ROM image for Hatari (you provide it).

[Select TOS image...](command:stosStudio.selectTosImage)

stosStudio.hardDrive.description: Folder Hatari uses as drive C:, relative to the project folder. Must be inside the project folder.

stosStudio.autoRun.description: Program Hatari starts automatically, as the Atari sees it.

stosStudio.stosFolder.markdownDescription:
Your own STOS folder (the one with `BASIC208.TOS`). Run copies it onto the emulated drive of a project once; a drive that already has STOS is left alone. STOS is not part of this extension.

[Select STOS folder...](command:stosStudio.selectStosFolder)

stosStudio.machine.markdownDescription: Atari model Hatari emulates. Pick a TOS image that fits it: TOS 1.02/1.04 for ST and Mega ST, TOS 1.62/2.06 for STE and Mega STE.

stosStudio.memory.description: ST RAM of the emulated Atari, in KB.

stosStudio.resolution.description: Screen resolution the Atari starts in. Most STOS games use low resolution.

stosStudio.codeFolder.markdownDescription: Folder on the emulated drive that gets your program (`MAIN.ASC`) and the assets, e.g. `CODE` gives `C:\CODE\MAIN.ASC`. Use a short Atari name (8 letters). Empty = the root of `C:`.

stosStudio.assetsFolder.markdownDescription: Folder of the project (sprite banks `.MBK`, pictures, data) whose files are copied onto the emulated drive on every Run, so a program can `load "sprites.mbk"`. Atari file names have 8 letters + 3. Empty = copy nothing.

stosStudio.toolkitFolder.markdownDescription:
Optional: your STOS-Toolkit folder (the separate project with the sprite editor and other graphic tools; it needs its `.venv`). Without it STOS Studio works as before, only the Toolkit commands are hidden.

[Select Toolkit folder...](command:stosStudio.selectToolkitFolder)

stosStudio.checkUnknownCommands.markdownDescription: Warn when a statement starts with a word that is not a known STOS command (for example a typo like `scren`).

stosStudio.checkParameterCounts.markdownDescription: Warn when a command gets too few or too many values (for example `sprite 1,100`). Only commands whose syntax line is plain are checked.

stosStudio.knownCommands.markdownDescription: Commands that STOS Studio does not know but your STOS has (for example from an extension), so they are not reported as unknown. One word or name per entry, such as `wave`.

stosStudio.buildToolkitGraphics.markdownDescription: Before Run copies the `assets` folder, let the STOS-Toolkit build the project's graphics, so they are current. Only happens with a Toolkit folder set and a `stos-toolkit.json` in the project; otherwise Run is unchanged. Files edited by hand are never overwritten.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Editing, help, colours and Build work. Run and the sprite editor start external programs (Hatari, Python), so they are disabled until you trust the workspace.
